newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Egypt briefs Arafat on summit with Israel.
newsitem.headline: Egypt briefs Arafat on summit with Israel.

text.p: Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak's adviser briefed Palestinian President Yasser Arafat on Wednesday on an Israeli-Egyptian summit that appeared to leave PLO officials unimpressed.
Osama al-Baz arrived in self-ruled Gaza a day after Mubarak met Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in a bid to revive stalled Israel-PLO peace talks.

The Israeli and Egyptian leaders, their countries partners to a 1979 treaty, made no breakthroughs but said their summit in the Egyptian resort of Sharm el-Sheikh would be followed by more talks on ending a two-month-old peacemaking crisis.
On Wednesday, Arafat's adviser Ahmed Tibi told Israel's army radio: "The crisis situation still exists. The ball is still in Mr Netanyahu's court."
A freeze of Jewish settlement construction in the West Bank is Arafat's condition for resuming talks with Israel but Netanyahu rules it out.
Egyptian Foreign Minister Amr Moussa said Cairo would await Netanyahu's response to issues raised at the summit before al-Baz shuttles between Israel and the Palestinians.

"Good will on Israel's part isn't enough to renew the peace talks. The Palestinians cannot accept a continuation of settlement activity -- and primarily in Jerusalem -- as a good will gesture," Moussa told Israel's Haaretz newspaper.
Mubarak said after the summit that he had discussed the issue of settlements with Netanyahu but they agreed any solution needed more talks.
The Egyptian leader said he hoped soon to bring the Palestinian leader into a three-way meeting with Israel.
But Tibi said there had been no positive change to bring about a Netanyahu-Arafat meeting.
Mubarak has suggested Israel halt work on an Arab East Jerusalem settlement, known as Har Homa and Jabal Abu Ghneim, for six months to give new momentum to peacemaking.
Israeli Foreign Minister David Levy declined comment on whether his country would accept a freeze in Jewish settlement.

But he told the radio on Wednesday: "I will say with certainty that if anyone expected Israel to come to Sharm el-Sheikh to accept all that was dictated to it, that did not happen and won't happen. If anyone thinks Israel will come and like a sphinx stand and say 'I have no alternative proposals', he too will be disappointed."

Levy said Netanyahu's inner security cabinet would on Wednesday hold the first of many discussions on its vision of a final peace deal with Palestinians. That accord, due to be completed in two years, will deal with the toughest issues such as borders, Jerusalem, settlements and Palestinian refugees.
